center.definition: least-squares circle centre of the OSM outer wall of Bldg 400 (relation 3126234); the infield roundabout centre is at (-1.3, -0.7) m and the inner-wall circle fit centre at (-1.5, -0.8) m

frame: x east, y north, metres; origin = ring centre; local equirectangular projection (cos(lat0) scaling), error < 1 cm over the site. For three.js use X = x, Z = -y (Y up). SCALE NOTE (verifier): the projection uses a spherical mean Earth radius R = 6371.0 km for both axes. Against WGS84 local radii at 41.7 N (meridional 6363.7 km, prime-vertical 6387.6 km), x (east) values are ~0.26% short and y (north) values ~0.12% long, i.e. up to ~0.5 m at 200 m from the centre. "<1 cm" refers to projection non-linearity only. This is irrelevant for the 3D map but matters if anyone compares against survey coordinates.

ring.electronOrbitRadiusNote: mean radius = C/2pi with APS-U C = 1103.6083 m (FDR Table 2.3); original APS design C = 1104 m, measured 1103.986 m
ring.idStraightApothemNote: perpendicular distance from ring centre to each ID straight line; geometric estimate 175.3 + 0.04*d m (d = half dipole spacing ~5 m) for a 40-fold ring of C~1104 m; APS-U kept the ID straights/tangent lines fixed (FDR 2-2.1.1, 3-4) VERIFIER: independent estimate from an equiangular 80-gon (exterior angle 4.5 deg, C = 1103.99 m pre-upgrade, since APS-U kept the ID tangent lines): h_ID = 175.62 - 0.0098*(L_ID - L_mid) m, L_ID - L_mid ~ 5-10 m -> 175.52-175.57 m; 175.5 +/- 0.15 m is consistent.
ring.hallInnerRadiusNote: inner (infield-facing) wall of the ring building = inner wall of the storage-ring tunnel; median of OSM inner-ring vertices excluding notches; circle fit r=169.3 m (rms 4.0 m, notches included); imagery roof edge ~169.5-170 m
ring.hallOuterRadiusNote: OSM outer wall (circle fit rms 0.04 m), consistent with roof edge in Esri imagery (~194-197 m incl. dark outer strip) and in the FDR Fig. 5.7 aerial photo. CONFLICT: APS Fast Facts says hall outer diameter is 1,225 ft (373 m -> r = 186.7 m); that cannot accommodate HEXM station D at 70-77 m from source (needs r >= 191.6 m), so the 1,225-ft figure is treated as approximate/other definition. VERIFIER: independent least-squares fit of OSM relation 3126234 outer way (258 nodes) reproduces centre lat/lon 41.703517, -87.988128 and r = 197.29 m (R = 6371.0 km scale; 197.4 +/- 0.4 m with WGS84 local radii; the OSM circle was evidently drawn with a circle tool, rms 0.04 m). Fast Facts PDF (PSC_16_6) does say "The outer diameter of the APS experiment hall is 1,225 feet" (373.4 m); with ID tangent lines at 175.5 m that would put the wall only ~64 m from the source along the beam, too short for the HEXM 20-ID-D hutch (instrument 70.2 m, beamstop 76.7 m, FDR Table 4.28). table.machineFunction: RF: 4 single-cell 352-MHz copper cavities (FDR 2019 2-3.10, ch.5). RF power is being moved from klystrons to solid-state amplifiers, one sector (4 cavities) at a time: the first sector was being installed in June 2026, full storage-ring deployment expected by 2028 (APS news 2026-06-10); the APS Strategic Plan 2025-29 orders the work sector 36, then 40, then 37.

RF: 4 single-cell 352-MHz copper cavities (FDR 2019 2-3.10, ch.5). RF power is being moved from klystrons to solid-state amplifiers, one sector (4 cavities) at a time: the first sector was being installed in June 2026, full storage-ring deployment expected by 2028 (APS news 2026-06-10); the APS Strategic Plan 2025-29 orders the work sector 36, then 40, then 37.

As built: passive (beam-driven) superconducting 4th-harmonic 1408-MHz bunch-lengthening cavity, 2.1 K, up to 1.3 MV, in one half of the 5-m straight (IPAC24 WEPS10); the other half holds the longitudinal bunch-by-bunch feedback kicker pair and the swap-out extraction stripline kickers (IPAC24 TUZN2 slides: "S38 longitudinal feedback kicker pair", "S38 Stripline Kickers Bakeout"; FDR 2-2.8.2: extraction kickers share the S38 straight with the harmonic cavity). The sector-38 main-RF cavities were removed (FDR ch.5).

Injection: DC Lambertson septum + 3 fast stripline injection kickers in the S39 ID straight (on-axis vertical swap-out injection); the replaced bunch is dumped in the swap-out dump inside S39A:M1 after a decoherence pre-kick and 3 extraction kicks in S38 (FDR 2-2.8, 2-3.x Table 2.29). World-first multi-bunch swap-out injection demonstrated 29 Apr 2024 (APS news 2024-04-30).

RF: 4 single-cell 352-MHz copper cavities (FDR 2019 2-3.10, ch.5). RF power is being moved from klystrons to solid-state amplifiers, one sector (4 cavities) at a time: the first sector was being installed in June 2026, full storage-ring deployment expected by 2028 (APS news 2026-06-10); the APS Strategic Plan 2025-29 orders the work sector 36, then 40, then 37.

linac.note: OSM tunnel 411 is ~70.7 m long, matching the "70m-long linear accelerator" (40-m electron linac + 30-m section) of Friedsam et al. (PAC95 TAA03). Guns at the east end (APS graphic "Linac" label); beam travels WSW into the injection wing 412. Original design: 200-MeV electron linac on a positron target + 450-MeV positron linac (APS tech. bulletin APS_1421579; Galayda PAC95 lists the electron linac as 250 MeV). Positrons are no longer used: today a thermionic RF gun feeds the ring and a photocathode RF gun feeds the LEA, with energies up to ~450 MeV (IBIC2023 WEP017); linac/PAR energy 425 -> 450+ MeV for APS-U (Calvey, I.FAST 2024); FDR 2-3.14.1 targets 450-500 MeV.

par.note: Particle (originally Positron) Accumulator Ring inside 412; position from the APS graphic (+/-3 m); circumference 30.667 m = 1/12 of booster (APS tech. bulletin APS_1421579; PAC95 "30.7-m")

booster.circumferenceSource: harmonic number 432 and RF 351.9149761 MHz (FDR Table 2.48) -> 368.0 m; also "synchrotron ring (SY) with a circumference of 368 m" (Friedsam et al. 1995)
booster.outlineMethod: dotted booster outline traced from the official APS "Beamline Disciplines and Locations" graphic (2026 web version), registered to OSM by 6 control points (rms ~2 m); r(theta) about the area centroid fitted with a robust 4th-order Fourier series (41 pts, 3 rejected, rms 0.4 m), then scaled from 362.2 m to the true circumference 368.02 m
booster.lattice: 40-cell FODO, zero-gradient dipoles; 12 dipoles deleted to make 4 zero-dispersion straights (Galayda, PAC95), so 68 dipoles (APS_1421579), giving a slightly squarish ring. Circumference 368 m = 1/3 of the storage ring (APS_1421579).
booster.energy: booster injection 325-500 MeV design range (FDR Table 2.48), in practice ~425-450 MeV; ramps to 6 GeV for APS-U (7 GeV before); repetition rate cut from 2 Hz to 1 Hz so the PAR can accumulate up to 20 nC for swap-out (FDR 2-3.14; Calvey, I.FAST 2024). The booster RF stays at 351.9149761 MHz, h = 432, while the ring runs at 352.056 MHz (FDR Table 2.48).
booster.outlineVerifierNote: The 1995 site plan (PAC95 Galayda Fig. 1) shows the booster as a near-circular oval in the north infield enclosing the RF/Extraction building, consistent with this outline; absolute position not independently checked (+/-5 m stands).

bts.note: SCHEMATIC ONLY (+/-5 m). Booster extraction is on the booster side nearest the ring (az ~100-118 deg, inside RF/Extraction wing 420); the BTS enters the ring tunnel, passes through three ring quadrupoles and clears the 38B:BM1 dipole (FDR 2-3.14.1.5) to reach the DC Lambertson septum in the sector-39 straight (FDR 2-2.8). (Not "short": the BTS runs from booster extraction near Bldg 420 through the ring tunnel to the S39 straight.)

lea.note: Linac Extension Area at the west end of the linac axis, beyond the booster: the former LEUTL enclosure, re-commissioned in 2023 as an accelerator R&D beamline (first beam at 425 MeV), reached via PAR-bypass, PAR-to-booster and booster-bypass lines (IBIC2023 WEP017).

plainLanguage.whatYouSee: The Advanced Photon Source is a doughnut-shaped building roughly 0.4 km across, about four American football fields end to end. (Map outlines give ~395 m; an APS fact sheet quotes 1,225 ft, or 373 m.) Inside it, in a shielded concrete tunnel, electrons race around a 1.1-km loop at almost the speed of light. Wherever magnets make them turn or wiggle, they give off X-rays that fly out along the tangent, like sparks off a grinding wheel, into 35 "sectors" of experiment stations on the outer floor.
plainLanguage.direction: Seen from above, the electrons go round clockwise, and sector numbers also count clockwise. Sector 1 is on the north-north-east side of the ring, next to the big office building 401. Sectors 19 and 20 are at the south: from there two extra-long beamlines run out to the separate Long Beamline Building in the south-west, where their experiments sit about 180 m and 220 m from the source.
plainLanguage.slices: The ring is divided like a pizza into 40 slices of 9 degrees. Slices 1-35 each have one straight section for undulators, the magnet arrays that make the brightest X-rays. In about 16 of them, two undulators are set at a tiny angle (1 milliradian) so that they feed two independent beamlines. About 16 sectors also run a beamline from a bending magnet. Slices 36-40 have no beamlines. Sectors 36, 37 and 40 hold the radio-frequency cavities that give the electrons back the energy they lose as X-rays. Sector 38 holds the bunch-lengthening cavity and the kickers that pull out a depleted bunch, and sector 39 holds the injection magnets that put a fresh, full bunch in its place ("swap-out").
plainLanguage.injector: In the infield, the hole of the doughnut, sits the injector. A ~70-m linear accelerator (building 411) speeds electrons to about 0.45 GeV and fires them into a small 31-m "particle accumulator ring" (in building 412), which gathers them into one dense bunch. A 368-m booster synchrotron then ramps the bunch to 6 GeV, about once per second, and a transfer line carries it to the big ring at sector 39.
plainLanguage.lom: The saw-toothed buildings around the outside are Lab/Office Modules (LOMs 431-438), plus Building 441 for sectors 25-27. Each serves 3-5 neighbouring sectors with labs and offices for the scientists (APS sector-location page).

openQuestions: sector1AngleDeg = 69.8 +/- 1.0 deg (hard bound 68.6-70.25 from LBB end-station containment, reproduced by the verifier; the verifier's corridor-position check gives 69.4). No public survey coordinate list or CAD plan with sector lines was found; an APS survey/alignment drawing would pin it to <0.1 deg.
Super-door <-> sector mapping (A=2, B=10, C=17, D=24, E=30) is inferred from OSM notch azimuths + FDR Fig. 5.7 labels; it assumes the doors sit opposite ID straights.

Experiment-hall outer wall: OSM/imagery give r = 197.3 m (diameter 394.6 m) but APS Fast Facts says 1,225 ft (373 m) diameter. The OSM circle may include an outer corridor; the hall floor must reach at least r ~ 192 m (HEXM station D at ~77 m from source).
Storage-ring tunnel width and ratchet-wall tooth geometry are not in the public documents found; 178 m is an estimate from front-end exit distances.
All building heights are guesses (no OSM height/levels tags). Photos or LIDAR (e.g. USGS 3DEP for DuPage County) would fix them.
Booster outline (+/-5 m) comes from a schematic graphic; the BTS path is schematic. A published injector layout drawing would improve this.

Zone-F as-built: RF in 36/37/40 and injection in 39 are confirmed; for sector 38, IPAC24 TUZN2 slides name the S38 longitudinal-feedback kicker pair and S38 stripline kickers, and IPAC24 WEPS10 puts the BLS in the same straight as the feedback kickers. So the BLS is almost certainly in S38, but no document found names "S38" and "BLS" in the same sentence.

Nomenclature: FDR Fig. 2.17 places "the ID straight of sector N" at the downstream end of accelerator sector N; this dossier assumes beamline N-ID uses that straight (standard usage) - confirm with an APS lattice/floor file.
Unidentified annex on the inner (infield) side of the ring at az 14-37 deg, r ~159-170 m (OSM inner-wall bulge; visible in imagery).
Fast-facts style numbers for the Experiment Assembly Area (Zone F floor) and the 401 main control room location are from 1995/2026 graphics labels, not from a floor plan.
ISN length quoted as 250 m by the builder vs instrument at 220 m (FDR / APS news); the 250 m likely includes the end-station hutch/beamstop or rounding.
ISN M3: the FDR design reflection angle is 2.5 mrad (5.0 mrad = 0.29 deg turn, used here); the as-built angle was not found.
LBB footprint: the OSM outline (1,458 m2) is ~22-29% smaller than the official 20,000-22,000 sq ft. Either the official figure includes corridors or a mezzanine, or the OSM outline is incomplete.
Which sectors have operating BM beamlines and canted branches in 2026 comes from the APS phone/location list and FDR 2019 tables. Check against the APS beamline directory before drawing BM fans.

threejsHints.axes: three.js X = x (east), Z = -y (south positive), Y = up. Ring centre at origin.
threejsHints.ring: Extrude buildings[id=400] polygon with its hole (or build the annulus procedurally from hallInnerRadiusM/hallOuterRadiusM). Electron orbit: circle r=175.64 m (or 40-gon through idSourceXY).
threejsHints.beams: Draw each sector ID beam from idSourceXY along idBeamDirDeg; x-rays travel clockwise. Typical in-hall beamlines end 55-80 m from the source; ISN/HEXM continue into Bldg 444. Draw BM beams only where bmBeamline2026 is non-null. For canted sectors (idFrontEndFDR2019) the two ID branches diverge by only 1 mrad; they are separated further by mirrors in the first optics enclosure.
threejsHints.scale: Whole site fits in ~700 m x 650 m; a camera at ~600 m height shows everything.
